## The catch: a FALSE `skip-artifact-only` verdict, and why it mattered

Gate run 4's first launch exited in under 3 seconds with verdict `skip-artifact-only` and sha
`2df589035bff108016980ad49076c111505c8480`. That sha is `origin/main` — the gate had certified MAIN,
not the branch. Trusting it would have merged this branch with ZERO lint certification, which is
precisely the failure the gate exists to prevent.

Mechanism: the composed gate script uses `git -C "$WT"` throughout but NEVER assigns `$WT` — it
inherits `REPO_ROOT` and `WT` from the caller, because the canonical Step 10d context has them from
the guard prelude. My detached `setsid nohup bash <script>` launch carried neither, so `git -C ""`
resolved against cwd (the repo root), `origin/main...HEAD` there was main-vs-main = an EMPTY diff,
and the artifact-only branch fired. The materialized own-diff file confirms it: 0 lines on the bad
run, 11 lines on the corrected one.

Two things are worth naming beyond my own mistake:
  1. This is a FAIL-OPEN in a gate. An unset `WT` produces a benign-looking `skip-artifact-only`
     rather than a loud refusal, and the verdict file's second line (the certified sha) is the only
     tell that the wrong tree was measured. A caller-contract assertion — refuse when `WT` is unset,
     or when the resolved worktree's HEAD equals `origin/main` — would convert a silent
     wrong-tree certification into a crash. Prose-only per the recursion guard (this session runs
     under a `workflow_fix_target:` line, so it files nothing further).
  2. My `$!` after `setsid nohup ... &` captured the setsid WRAPPER, which exits immediately once it
     forks — so the pid I recorded was already dead and reported `alive? NO` while the gate itself
     was fine. Corrected form: `setsid nohup bash -c 'echo $$ > <pidfile>; exec bash <script>' &`,
     where `exec` preserves the pid so the breadcrumb names the real process.
